title: CTO Interview with Dr. Valerio Tenace of ChipNexus
gist: Interview with ChipNexus CTO Valerio Tenace: the startup (formerly PrimisAI) evolved from natural-language-to-RTL generation into agentic AI covering the whole chip design stack via its hierarchical multi-agent Nexus/NEX AI platform, and is now building proprietary in-house models. He argues time to market is the core customer pain, general-purpose assistants fall short on reliability, EDA context and local-execution IP needs, and engineers will shift toward supervising AI agents.

insights.claim: ChipNexus, formerly PrimisAI, began in late 2021 by automating the path from natural-language specifications to synthesizable RTL and now claims its solutions cover the entire silicon design stack.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Shows AI-for-EDA startups expanding from point tools (RTL generation) toward full-flow automation, putting them on a collision course with incumbent EDA vendors.
insights.quote: Today, our solutions cover the entire design stack.

insights.claim: In late 2023 ChipNexus built Nexus, an open-source hierarchical multi-agent LLM system for hardware design that decomposes complex engineering tasks and routes each sub-task to the best-suited agent.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Hierarchical multi-agent orchestration is emerging as the architecture of choice for agentic EDA; watch for incumbents adopting similar designs.
insights.quote: We gave it a hierarchical structure so it can break a complex engineering task into smaller units of work and route each one to the agent best suited to handle it.
insights.locator: Why is your approach to solving this problem unique?

insights.claim: ChipNexus is developing proprietary in-house AI models aimed at speeding the most time-consuming tasks in the chip design flow, with details promised in the coming weeks.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: A move from open-source orchestration to proprietary models signals an attempt to build defensible IP/moat; watch for the announcement.
insights.locator: More recently, we’ve been developing proprietary AI models

insights.claim: Time to market is the biggest challenge for chip design customers, driven by spec definition, keeping documentation in sync, architectural exploration, verification at every stage, and migrating designs to new process nodes, where changes cascade into rework elsewhere.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Tools that reduce cross-flow rework (not just single-step speedups) target the largest cost lever in chip development.
insights.quote: Needless to say, changes in one part of the design flow often trigger rework elsewhere.
insights.locator: What is the biggest challenge your customer is facing?

themes.theme: Limits of general-purpose AI in silicon

insights.claim: General-purpose AI assistants are insufficient for silicon design because errors introduced early propagate downstream and become more expensive to fix, and assistants need precise knowledge of a team's EDA tools, IP blocks and design guidelines.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Supports a domain-specific AI-for-EDA thesis over horizontal LLM assistants in semiconductor design.
insights.quote: an error introduced early can propagate downstream, where it becomes harder and more expensive to fix
insights.locator: What other approaches are being used to solve this problem?

insights.claim: Most chip companies need to keep design IP inside their own environments, making local execution of AI tools essential and an engineering challenge in its own right.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: On-prem/local deployment capability is a gating requirement for AI EDA vendors selling to chip firms, favoring vendors who can run models locally.
insights.quote: For those teams, local execution is essential and that alone brings its own engineering challenges.
insights.locator: Giving a language model the right context

insights.claim: As AI agents take on design work, hardware engineers will shift into a supervisory role — defining problems, setting constraints and giving feedback — making deep hardware expertise more, not less, important to catch flawed assumptions in AI proposals.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Suggests AI in EDA augments rather than replaces scarce design talent; seat-based value may shift toward supervision workflows.
insights.quote: In some ways, I see the hardware engineer taking on the role of a supervisor.
insights.locator: What challenges will your customers face in the near future?

insights.claim: ChipNexus steers its product roadmap by observing which tasks engineers repeatedly use its tools for and where they intervene to guide the system.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Usage-telemetry-driven roadmaps indicate the product is still finding its highest-value use cases.
insights.locator: How has AI changed your business strategy?
